events.finding: KDemo daily archive identifies Lee Byeong-do press conference, threat of coercive response, and union rebuttal invoking Constitution article 13 and labor law.
Jo Il-mun stated that administrative litigation would follow concrete sanctions and that Civil Service Act article 37 should be amended as inconsistent with constitutional spirit.
Union and allied labor officials expressly invoked Labor Union Act article 6 as permitting organization and planned coordinated resistance to transfers.
Union statement specified 397 transfers and alleged Education Public Officials Act article 30 and Labor Union Act article 10 violations; treated as union legal claim, not adjudicated fact.
About 2,000 participants; Kang Gi-cheol threatened collective resignation/class refusal; legal and academic figures plus public-sector unions expressed support.
National Assembly debate exposed distinct legislative positions: outright opposition, pro-union questioning, and Oh Cheon-seok's organization-permitted/strike-right-denied government position.
Gyeongbuk union identified Kwak Tae-jin et al. as sponsors of a bill perceived as illegalizing teachers' unions and threatened fasting action.
Hundreds of regional teachers-union delegates demonstrated at the National Assembly against an illegalization provision; date discrepancy in contemporaneous reporting explicitly noted by archive.
KDemo dictionary says Education Ministry drafted a separate Teachers' Organization Bill and sent it to State Council Secretariat review; do not merge with Labor Union Act amendment.
Four education-establishment figures alleged violence/coercion by union members; preserved as attributed allegation pending police/school/union records.
ICFTU letter reportedly supported teachers' organizing rights under Korean and international law; classified as external advocacy, not domestic adjudication.
Union criticized police summons of delegates for building-entry allegations after Jan 16-17 sit-in; criminal-file target opened.
About 600 delegates demanded withdrawal of Two Evil Laws, release/reversal of measures against unionists, and issuance of union registration certificate.

adversarial_findings: The executive branch was not internally uniform in May-June 1960: Lee Hang-nyeong, Lee Byeong-do and Kim Hak-muk are reported with materially different positions.
The teachers' union itself cited multiple statutory bases at different stages; its legal claims must not be converted into court holdings.
The 397-transfer figure is stronger than generic 'about 400' reporting but still derives from union statement indexed from newspapers; original personnel orders remain required.
The September Labor Union Act amendment track and the Education Ministry Teachers' Organization Bill track are distinct and must not be collapsed.
The National Assembly debate demonstrates multiple individual legislators' positions, preventing attribution of a single view to 'the Assembly' or 'the Democratic Party'.
The October 19 allegations by Korean Education Association figures provide an adversarial source against a one-sided union narrative but remain allegations until independently corroborated.
ICFTU support establishes international advocacy/provenance, not binding interpretation of Korean law.
Later 1961 criminal prosecution cannot retroactively settle the legality of 1960 organizing.
The KDemo archive itself flags a date discrepancy for the Sept. 29 sit-in, so event dating retains provenance note.
The alleged 1959 Justice Ministry interpretation remains unresolved and cannot be inferred from the 1960 executive positions.
